title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
abstract: arXiv:2610.23673v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-criteria models for healthcare operations need weights that express how stakeholders trade off patient waiting time, provider workload, and operating cost, but these weights are difficult to quantify. Teams of large language model (LLM) agents, each prompted to represent a stakeholder, have been used to supply them. We propose a framework for assessing the reliability of LLM-generated preferences as inputs to multi-objective optimization and quantifying how their uncertainty affects decisions. We study explicit preferences by asking agents to rate the importance of the criteria in an outpatient appointment scheduling problem, and implicit preferences by inferring trade-offs from the agents' pairwise choices between emergency department configurations. translated_title: 关于基于大语言模型的多智能体系统在医疗运营管理多准则决策中的可能性与局限性
translated_abstract: 医疗运营的多准则模型需要权重来表达利益相关者如何在患者等待时间、服务提供者工作负荷和运营成本之间进行权衡，但这些权重难以量化。由大型语言模型（LLM）智能体组成的团队（每个智能体被设定为代表一名利益相关者）已被用于提供这些权重。我们提出了一个框架，用于评估LLM生成的偏好作为多目标优化输入的可靠性，并量化其不确定性对决策的影响。我们通过让智能体对门诊预约调度问题中各准则的重要性进行评分来研究显式偏好，并通过从智能体在急诊科配置之间的成对选择中推断权衡关系来研究隐式偏好。计算实验表明，显式偏好会响应诊所的运营条件并在不同角色之间存在差异，但智能体之间的 deliberation 可能会消除这些差异……
tldr: 本研究提出了一个评估LLM生成偏好作为多目标优化输入可靠性的框架，发现显式偏好能响应诊所运营条件并在不同利益相关者角色间存在差异，但智能体之间的集体审议可能抹平这些差异。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a framework for assessing the reliability of LLM-generated preferences as inputs to multi-objective optimization in healthcare operations, finding that explicit preferences respond to clinic operating conditions and vary across stakeholder roles, but deliberation among agents can erase these differences.
